correctness.rationale: PASS. The contradiction is genuine. In characteristic two with an involution of the second kind, the source identifies Hermitian and alternate-Hermitian scalar parts; for D=F4 with star(x)=x^2 the fixed field is F2 and therefore AH_2(F4)=H_2(F4). The source's Hermitian n=2, |D|=4 classification gives the explicit nonlocal range-compatible Phi_0 and all additive range-compatible maps as a local map plus Phi_0 alpha, while its alternate-Hermitian theorem separately recognizes n=2, |D|=4 as the exceptional additive case. Yet Theorem 1.7(a) of the inspected v1 states without that exception that every admissible F-linear map on AH_n(D) is local. Because every additive map of F2-vector spaces is F2-linear, Phi_0 directly contradicts that sentence. Local maps are parametrized by X in F4^2 and Phi_0 F4 meets them trivially, so the direct-sum space has 4^3=64 maps, of which 4^2=16 are local and 48 nonlocal. I independently reran a complete enumeration of all 2^16 F2-linear maps from the four-dimensional domain to F4^2; exactly 64 were range-compatible, exactly 16 local, and the classified family matched all 64 with no extras or omissions.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified. The exceptional map Phi_0 and Hermitian classification are explicitly prior results of the same source; the contribution is the internal contradiction with its unconditional Theorem 1.7(a), the corrected alternate-Hermitian statement, and the exact 64/16/48 count. Targeted searches through September 29 found no public erratum or indexed later paper making this correction. A third-party index reports a September 18 metadata update, but the full theorem text inspected for the record is v1, so very recent author-side revision remains a residual priority risk.

scientific_value.rationale: PASS. Correcting a false unconditional classification theorem in a current algebra preprint has direct scientific value, especially because the exception is not merely existential: the record gives the complete exceptional family and an exhaustive finite verification. This prevents downstream use of Theorem 1.7(a) in precisely the smallest second-kind finite-field case.
